articles.title: Swedish army to get recon, strike drones in $37M deal
articles.body:
- Sweden ordered its first strike drones, a $37 million contract with Danish company Nordic Wing for Astero ISR and Raptor 2 systems.
- Delivery is planned for the second quarter of 2027, with the systems intended primarily for Swedish ground forces.
Sweden has placed its first order for strike drones for its armed forces, awarding a contract to Danish company Nordic Wing through the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration, Militarnyi reported.
The deal is worth 350 million Swedish krona, approximately $37 million, according to the Swedish agency. Delivery to Swedish forces is planned for the second quarter of 2027.
The order covers the Astero ISR reconnaissance drone and Raptor 2 loitering munitions, which operate through shared software. The reconnaissance drone is intended to locate targets, after which one or more strike drones can engage them, according to the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration.
The purchase also includes control stations built around laptops and radio equipment, operator training simulators, and field-deployable maintenance containers. The systems are intended primarily for Sweden’s ground forces, the agency said.
“This system provides new capabilities, particularly for light units, to engage targets at long range with a combat unit that has very high effectiveness,” said Lennart Widerström, head of the Swedish Army’s Combat School.
Widerström said Swedish forces are prepared to receive the new drones and will be able to quickly begin using them for defense.
“We want this capability because it’s a natural part of modern warfare,” Widerström said.
The Swedish armed forces described the purchase as a first step, with plans to acquire additional unmanned systems from multiple manufacturers going forward. The decision to order strike drones is tied to lessons from the war in Ukraine, which Swedish military officials have closely followed, according to Militarnyi.
Nordic Wing’s drones have already been supplied to Ukraine’s Defense Forces for several years, according to Militarnyi’s prior reporting.

articles.title: Indonesia and China discuss increasing defense cooperation and energy security
articles.body:
Indonesia and China discuss increasing defense cooperation and energy security
JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Top ministers for Indonesia and China agreed during meetings in Jakarta on Friday to increase their defense cooperation and strengthen food and energy security.
The meetings come as Jakarta deepens military ties with China while trying to maintain its long-standing non-aligned foreign policy and balance relations with other major powers.
China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Indonesia and China agreed to better coordinate on their top development and security priorities as the two countries modernize.
Wang said the dialogue will “send a clear signal to the world of solidarity and cooperation between our two major emerging-market countries.”
Indonesian Foreign Minister Sugiono said the two sides discussed strengthening food, energy and mineral security through the development of industries that support national resilience, which in the future will encompass areas such as artificial intelligence, the joint development of communications satellites and other advanced technology initiatives.
“We also agreed to facilitate trade, including market exploration and the expansion of market access for Indonesia’s flagship commodities,” Sugiono, who uses one name, said in a jointly released statement.
The countries’ defense ministers, Indonesia’s Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin and China’s Dong Jun, met separately and discussed intensifying defense cooperation.
“We also invite the Chinese armed forces to participate in joint exercises, such as the Heping Garuda exercise, which is a concrete example of the relationship between the Indonesian National Armed Forces and the Chinese armed forces,” Sjamsoeddin said.
He added that Indonesia and China will collaborate on a joint munitions factory in Indonesia, which will also produce missiles and rockets. China will transfer technology to Indonesia as part of the plan, which is set to begin in 2027.
Indonesia’s economic ties with China have flourished in recent years, reaching about $167 billion in 2025.
China has become Indonesia’s largest trading partner and plowed billions into major infrastructure projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung high-speed railway and Cirata, Southeast Asia’s largest floating solar power project, on a reservoir in West Java, 130 kilometers (80 miles) from the capital, Jakarta.
Disagreements have emerged over the pricing and timing for the projects, but China says it is determined to follow through on them in keeping with President Xi Jinping’s signature “Belt and Road” initiative to build infrastructure throughout the region.

Associated Press video producer Olivia Zhang in Beijing contributed to this report.

articles.title: Perm industrial facility comes under attack: 325 drones target Russian regions
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 21. /TASS/. Russian air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 325 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over Russian regions and the waters of the Black and Azov seas overnight, the Defense Ministry said.
Damage was reported at an industrial facility in the Perm Region.
TASS has compiled the key facts about the consequences of the attack.
Attack scale
- From 8 p.m. Moscow time on August 20 to 8 a.m. Moscow time on August 21 (5 p.m. GMT on August 20 - 5 a.m. GMT on August 21), air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 325 Ukrainian fixed-wing UAVs, the Defense Ministry said.
- The drones were intercepted over the Astrakhan, Belgorod, Bryansk, Volgograd, Voronezh, Kaluga, Kursk, Oryol, Rostov, Ryazan, Tula, Moscow, Krasnodar and Perm Regions, as well as over Crimea, Udmurtia, and the waters of the Azov and Black seas.
- More than 30 drones were destroyed overnight in four districts of the Rostov Region, Governor Yury Slyusar said.
- Sixteen Ukrainian drones were shot down over the Perm Region, Governor Dmitry Makhonin said.
Aftermath
- Damage was reported at an industrial facility in the Perm Region, but no one was injured, Makhonin said.
- A man sustained shrapnel wounds in a drone attack in the region. He remains in stable condition.
- A kamikaze drone hit a residential house in the village of Voronok in the Starodubsky district of the Bryansk Region, acting Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said.
- A local resident sustained shrapnel wounds in the blast.
- A man was also injured in a drone attack in the village of Ponurovka in the Starodubsky district.
- All those injured received immediate medical assistance.
- Ukrainian forces used a UAV to strike a multifamily building in the Kalininsky district of Gorlovka in the Donetsk People's Republic, city Mayor Ivan Prikhodko said. There were no casualty reports.
- A woman and her two-year-old child were injured in a Ukrainian attack on Sevastopol in the evening, city Governor Mikhail Razvozhayev said.
- The child sustained superficial chest injuries from fragments of roofing slate after debris from a downed UAV landed on the roof.
- The child's mother was also injured by shrapnel.

articles.title: 160 grams, 118-km link, and jam-resistance by frequency-hopping: Ukraine’s answer to drone war’s connectivity problem
articles.body:
A Ukrainian company has built a drone link designed to keep working when the enemy tries to jam it. Ukraine's defense-tech firm Rise Technologies has developed the Nakande digital communication system, designed for rapid integration into small and large FPV drones, bombers, and fixed-wing platforms, commercial director Viktor Chuikovskyi says, Defender Media reports.
The system attacks the connectivity problem that jamming creates for Ukraine's drones. On a front saturated with electronic warfare, drones that lose their radio link become useless, and Nakande answers that by constantly hopping frequencies to find clear air.
How the frequency-hopping works
Nakande's defining feature is its ability to change frequency. It hops across a tuning range of up to 1,000 MHz, monitoring channels within that band, finding a freer stretch, and automatically switching to it, Chuikovskyi said, which lets operators keep their link to drones amid electronic warfare and a congested radio spectrum.
That is the core countermeasure to jamming. By moving to whatever frequency is clear rather than staying on one the enemy can block, the system stays connected where a fixed-frequency link would be jammed dead.
What the link carries
Nakande's airborne module weighs 160 grams, supports 2×Ethernet and MAVLink, and combines control, telemetry, and video in a single secure link, with a downlink up to 5.2 Mbit/s that the maker says delivers clean video and a compressed 4K stream, protected by AES-256 encryption.
It is built for fast, flexible setup. The ground station deploys in under five minutes. Its standard IP architecture allows the operator, antenna, and control point to be separated over Ethernet, fiber, or VPN, and a single ground station can connect 50 to 100 modules.
It held a link past 100 kilometers
Nakande has been tested in combat, the maker says. It passed bench, field, and combat checks, with a dedicated range class up to 60 kilometers for FPV drones, and in testing its maximum configuration, held a link at 118 kilometers, Chuikovskyi said.
The company did not disclose the module's price but said it is several times lower than foreign equivalents.

As Washington decides to isolate Tehran economically, Iran-Oman talks are in crisis
At a time when everyone was awaiting the outcome of talks between Iran and Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, hoping that any potential understanding would help move forward stalled diplomacy between Tehran and Washington, US President Donald Trump announced on Thursday morning, 20 August, the launch of the strongest economic operation ever against Iran.
The US decision raises questions about the prospects of Iranian-Omani talks over the Strait of Hormuz and whether these new sanctions will derail them.
On Wednesday, the United States said it was not currently holding any negotiations with Iran, and argued that a huge amount of oil was passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran, for its part, responded to the new US decision. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a post on X on Thursday that insisting on continuing "failed policies" would only lead to further failures and bring about the enmity of Iranians.
He added that "US economic terrorism" threatens the global economy and the national sovereignty of countries around the world.
His deputy for international affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, also said in a post on X that "the military war proved ineffective, and now they have called the next defeat an economic war".
The new US tactic comes after the Iranian foreign minister affirmed on 17 August during a telephone discussion with his Turkish counterpart, Hakan Fidan, his country's determination to continue talks with Muscat on determining an appropriate route for ships to pass "safely" through the Strait of Hormuz.
Araghchi also said in an interview with the Iranian newspaper Shahrara News that negotiations with Oman were ongoing, adding that it was a technical and specialised process concerning the definition of shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz for ships to pass through.
He explained that the routes that previously existed were no longer valid and that a new route had to be defined, noting that work was underway to design a temporary route that would become the final route at later stages.
"We may reach a result soon, but I need to emphasise that these negotiations and the issue of opening the Strait of Hormuz are two completely separate discussions," he said, further noting that opening the strait is subject to other conditions that the United States must meet for that to happen.
Where do Iran-Oman talks stand?
Iranian expert Ali Qalehki told The New Arab that Iran's position on the Strait of Hormuz had become "more offensive" after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met earlier this month with Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, as well as after the appointment of Maj Gen Mohsen Rezaei as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.
He added that the strait would only be opened when Iran was able to restore its rights in various areas in exchange for reopening it.
He argued that Iran wants to consolidate a system for imposing fees on passing ships and providing services to them, with the route through the strait to be "entirely based on an Iranian mechanism and from the northern side, which is something the Americans do not like".
The Iranian expert explained that negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz were "currently suspended" and that the United States "was the main party that disrupted" this negotiating track.
He noted that Iranian-Omani negotiations had been discussing the establishment of a shipping route whereby entry into the Strait of Hormuz would be through the Iranian route, meaning Iranian territorial waters, while 60% of the exit or return route would pass through the Omani route and 40% through the Iranian route.
According to Qalehki, the Iranian side later insisted that the return route also be entirely through the Iranian route, noting that Oman agreed to this.
However, the recent US threat to bomb Oman ultimately led to the disruption of the new agreement on the shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz.
Qalehki continued that reaching an agreement on Hormuz "is the most distant option for Tehran at present, but if the United States accepts Iran's conditions, which is unlikely, then an agreement on the strait will be reached".
Regarding these conditions, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said last Tuesday that Hormuz would not be opened unless the US implemented its commitments under the memorandum of understanding concluded last June, including lifting the blockade, releasing frozen funds, lifting oil sanctions, ending threats and military operations on all fronts, and "the rest of the conditions that Washington committed to".
War after November?
Iranian expert on Iranian-US relations Esfandiar Khodai told TNA that his country was keeping the strait closed because it did not want to lose this leverage.
He said that if Iran did not exert pressure on the United States, sanctions would continue easily, the blockade would continue, and Iran would be exposed to war and attack.
Khodai noted that Tehran was therefore using the strait as leverage, adding that Iran's negotiating party over the Strait of Hormuz was not only Oman but also that the presence of diplomacy with Oman was "important" so that the diplomatic channel would not be closed.
He stressed that the main party in these negotiations was the United States, while ruling out any direct connection between the US decision to economically isolate Iran and the talks between Tehran and Muscat over a new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz.
Regarding the impact of the US decision on these negotiations, Khodai said it would lead to stronger Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz.
"When the decision is that no ship should arrive, even if it is carrying food or medicine, there is no reason for Iran to open the strait," he added.
He explained that the negotiations the United States is conducting with Iran, whether through Oman or other parties, "are not aimed at reaching a solution; rather, they are aimed at gaining legitimacy and creating an atmosphere in which Washington says it negotiated with Iran, but the other side did not respond and was not prepared to negotiate or reach a deal".
Accordingly, Khodai expects the United States to return to war with Iran after the US primary elections in November, noting that the Israeli lobby is seeking to exploit Trump's presidency to complete the effort against Iran.
He said the lobby fears the period after Trump and a shift in US focus from the Middle East towards East Asia.
In this context, the expert on Iranian-US relations told The New Arab that what the US administration calls Iran's economic isolation "is not a new matter", noting that Iran is currently facing a naval blockade and economic war, in addition to the maximum sanctions that have been in place for years.
He further mulled that what Trump wants is to raise the level of escalation to its maximum so that restrictions also include items that had been relatively exempt, such as medicine and food.
He explained that the actual goal is to turn the existing naval blockade into a comprehensive economic war and bring sanctions to a crescendo.

articles.title: Commander-in-Chief Drapatyi announces NATO Military Committee visit to Ukraine in October
articles.body:
Commander-in-Chief Drapatyi announces NATO Military Committee visit to Ukraine in October
Mykhailo Drapatyi, Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, has said that the NATO Military Committee will visit Ukraine in October this year.
Source: European Pravda, citing Drapatyi's post on social media
Quote from Drapatyi: "Today [21 August – ed.], I spoke for the first time with the Chair of the NATO Military Committee, Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone… We expect the NATO Military Committee to visit Ukraine in October. The last such visit took place eight years ago."
Details: The commander-in-chief noted that the admiral has visited Ukraine three times and has seen the situation on the ground.
"I briefed him on the situation on the front and our priorities: long-range strikes, flexible infantry tactics and the use of robotic systems on the front line. We also discussed air defence separately. Protecting the skies is my priority," Drapatyi said.
Background:
- Earlier, commenting on Drapatyi's appointment as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, NATO stressed that the Alliance's strategy of supporting Ukraine remains clear and unwavering.
- A spokesperson for NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe also told European Pravda that a meeting between Drapatyi and General Alexus Grynkewich, Supreme Allied Commander Europe and Commander of US European Command, is only a matter of time, as NATO is devoting considerable attention to Ukraine's defence.

articles.title: Ukraine hits oil refinery and military airfield in Russia – video
articles.body:
Ukraine hits oil refinery and military airfield in Russia – video
The Ukrainian defence forces struck an oil refinery in the Russian city of Perm and the Marinovka military airfield in Russia's Volgograd Oblast on the night of 20-21 August.
Source: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on X (Twitter)
Quote: "We continue, through our long-range sanctions, to bring the consequences of the war back to where it came from.
Last night, our deep strikes hit an oil refinery in Perm, more than 1,600 km from the border, and the Marinovka military air base in Volgograd Oblast. There are also results in the Black Sea."
Details: The president also reported confirmed results from previous strikes: a Russian Su-34 aircraft was damaged at the Akhtubinsk airfield, around 600 km from the front line. In Primorsko-Akhtarsk, almost 180 km away, a site used to store, prepare and launch attack drones that Russia uses to strike Ukrainians was hit.
Background: On 21 August, drones attacked the Russian city of Perm, home to the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery. Air defence was active and an air-raid warning was issued in the city.

articles.title: Ex-defence minister Fedorov plans trip to US, but no meetings with politicians – Suspilne
articles.body:
Ex-defence minister Fedorov plans trip to US, but no meetings with politicians – Suspilne
Former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov is planning a trip to the United States in the near future. His team says it is unrelated to political meetings.
Source: Fedorov's press service in a comment to Suspilne, a Ukrainian public broadcaster
Details: Fedorov's team said the trip is related to defence tech projects.
Quote: "The main purpose of the trip which is potentially being planned is to attract resources for new projects in the field of defence tech."
Details: The press service stated that no meetings with American politicians or officials are scheduled.
The Kyiv Independent earlier reported that Fedorov may fly to the US as early as next week.
Meanwhile, The Guardian has suggested that the trip is intended to help drum up support from Washington for the idea of holding elections in Ukraine.
Background:
- In a public address on 18 August, Fedorov insisted that Russia cannot be allowed to determine when Ukrainians can once again elect their government.
- In March 2026, Zelenskyy stated that elections would take place "after the war is over, not during a temporary ceasefire".

articles.title: Ex-FSB general who wired Russia’s spies and army found dead in Moscow—a gunshot, no note, no official report
articles.body:
A retired Russian FSB major-general whose company built secure communications for the Kremlin's security services and military has been found dead in his Moscow apartment, RFE/RL's Current Time reported. Russian outlets, citing their own sources, say the 83-year-old apparently killed himself, though authorities have released nothing. His death adds to a run of senior Russian military and security figures dying in the capital.
An FSB veteran who wired Russia's spies
Igor Laptev, 83, was found dead in an apartment in Moscow. Russian outlet MK and others, citing sources, wrote that he probably took his own life on the afternoon of 20 August. Izvestia claimed he died from a gunshot wound to the head. No suicide note or motive has been reported, and Russian law enforcement has issued no official statement.
Laptev was a chemist-technologist by training who served in the Soviet KGB, including combat in Afghanistan, according to Delovoy Peterburg. In the KGB and later the FSB, he worked on information security. In the late 1990s, he was a deputy minister for taxes and duties, and from 1998, he chaired the board of Informtekhnika i Svyaz, now the Informtekhnika group.
A supplier to the FSB, the guards, and the army
The company says on its own site that it makes communications systems for federal authorities and security structures, including the FSB, the FSO federal guard service, the Defense Ministry, and the interior ministry. According to OSINT VARTA, it develops and produces specialized telecom equipment and software for secure communications, building switching systems and special-comms platforms for security agencies and state bodies. It also works with Voentelecom, a Russian Defense Ministry structure, to supply troops with digital telecom gear, Militarnyi reported.
A string of deaths among Russia's brass
Laptev's death is not the first in Moscow involving retired Russian generals. On 2 May, retired colonel-general Stanislav Petrov — founder of Russia's radiological, chemical and biological defense troops, who helped create the TOS-1 Buratino heavy flamethrower system — was found dead in a central Moscow apartment. Weeks ago, Moscow buried a general under roadblocks and metal detectors after a bombing that likely killed him at a commander's gathering.

articles.title: New York woman charged in plot to set off explosives at state Capitol, kill lawmakers, FBI says
articles.body:
New York woman charged with plotting to set off explosives at state Capitol, kill lawmakers
A woman who authorities said had been plotting to bomb the New York State Capitol building because she believed laws were being passed that were an affront to Islam was caught in an FBI sting operation and is now facing a federal terrorism charge, authorities announced Thursday.
Jessica Bowie, 35, of Albany, had been under surveillance for more than a month as she communicated with at least one confidential informant posing as an ISIS facilitator, according to a criminal complaint.
Operatives working for the FBI then facilitated her plans, including providing her with money to buy ingredients for a nail bomb. On Wednesday, according to the complaint, the operatives handed Bowie a gun, ammunition and an inert explosive, then gave her instructions on how to use them.
FBI agents then arrested Bowie as she left that meeting with the weapons in a bag, authorities said.
No attorney information was listed for Bowie. The Federal Public Defenders’ office in Albany declined to comment Thursday.
After her arrest, Bowie told FBI agents during an interview that she expected to go to prison, according to the criminal complaint.
“There’s no helping me, you guys know enough,” she said, according to an FBI agent’s account.
John Sarcone, first assistant U.S. attorney for the Northern District of New York, called the alleged plot “an attack on democracy itself and one we will not tolerate.”
Court documents said Bowie had converted to Islam about five years ago. The affidavit of probable cause said FBI counterterrorism agents saw a number of online accounts linked back to Bowie in which she had expressed support for terrorism in posts starting around May.
Agents began monitoring those accounts and became aware starting around July 16 that Bowie wanted to carry out an attack on the state Capitol, the criminal complaint said. She asked for lessons from one informant on how to build an explosive device, made at least five trips to the Capitol grounds to plan where it might be most effective to set off an explosive, and scoped out security measures all while in contact with multiple informants, authorities said.
Pictures of Bowie conducting reconnaissance at the Capitol and buying a list of bomb-making ingredients at a hardware store — including long nails for shrapnel — were included in the affidavit. She also arranged to buy a firearm and ammunition in order to fire the weapon at police or security if needed, authorities said.
“Ms. Bowie did not just plan to kill lawmakers, she wanted a complete disruption of our government,” said Craig L. Tremaroli, special agent in charge of the FBI’s Albany Field Office.
Tremaroli said she planned to flee the country after the attack, but said she would be willing to return to launch more attacks on the White House or on Times Square on New Year’s Eve.
The affidavit also noted Bowie had considered making Albany City Hall a target, but had settled on the Capitol and specifically targeted state senators because they make laws that she considered to be offensive to Islam. The legislature has been out of session since June.
Gov. Kathy Hochul’s office released a statement Thursday, saying the state had taken steps earlier this year to strengthen security across state government, including at the Capitol, amid a rise nationally in political violence and threats against public officials.
“While there is no immediate threat at this time, we will continue working closely with our law enforcement partners to protect New Yorkers and keep our communities safe,” she wrote.
